title: PowerPoint on desktop: reference webpages when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Windows release-note entry is titled Reference web sources when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint and carries roadmap ID 555896.
claims.quote:
**Reference web sources when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint** [Windows]

You can now ask Copilot in PowerPoint to reference relevant online sources while creating a presentation.

**Roadmap ID:**[555896]

claims.claim: The release notes place the entry in the July 28 to August 11, 2026 update window.
claims.quote:
## August 11, 2026

Updates released between July 28, 2026, and August 11, 2026.

claims.claim: Users can ask Copilot to reference relevant online sources while creating a presentation.
claims.quote: You can now ask Copilot in PowerPoint to reference relevant online sources while creating a presentation.

claims.claim: The feature's release-note entry does not mention Agent Mode.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Agent Mode' in the opened release-note entry for 555896 at learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes; the entry describes presentation creation without that term.

claims.claim: The release notes do not specify whether users supply page addresses or Copilot selects the sources.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Copilot reference webpages default enabled'; opened release-notes, entry 555896. It says to request a topic benefiting from current web information, without specifying supplied URLs or source selection.

claims.claim: No additional Learn feature page explains how this capability fetches or cites webpages.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Copilot reference webpages default enabled'; 'PowerPoint Copilot web sources approval source references retention'. Read release-notes and returned excerpts; no separate page explaining this in-app feature's fetch/citation mechanism.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is Microsoft's primary administrative web-search control and is available in Cloud Policy service.
claims.quote: The primary way that IT admins can control access to web search is by using the **Allow web search in Copilot** policy, which is available only in [Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365]

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0]
claims.claim: The policy controls web search for users or user groups across the tenant in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center route is Copilot > Settings > Data access > Web search for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, expand **Copilot**, and then select **Settings**.
3. Browse **User access**, **Data access**, **Copilot actions**, and **Other settings**.
claims.fix: Keep the documented entry-point path, but complete its note: 'Follow the link to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, then Customization > Policy Management > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy for the continuation. The existing route stops at the correct setting's link rather than the policy itself.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the web-search setting through an applyOnce baseline.
claims.quote: Create a new [configurationMonitor] object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in `monitorOnly` mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in `applyOnce` mode.

claims.claim: The request body's mode property accepts applyOnce.
claims.quote: | mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: `monitorOnly`, `applyOnce`, `unknownFutureValue`. Optional; defaults to `monitorOnly`. |

claims.claim: microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch is the baseline resource that controls web search.
The web-search resource's value property accepts 0, 1 or 2.
claims.quote: `0` enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. `1` disables it in both. `2` disables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Work mode while enabling it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Web mode and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The Graph automation is preview and uses beta.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: Creating the applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only.
claims.quote: Creating an `applyOnce` monitor supports delegated permissions only.

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: A group-level policy configuring the same setting makes TCM applyOnce fail for that resource.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and `applyOnce` fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The documented TCM applyOnce capability is for the global service, not national clouds.
claims.quote: TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.
claims.fix: Replace 'It is for the global service, not national clouds' with 'The TCM remediation and applyOnce support page limits the capability to the global service; the Create configurationMonitor reference separately lists endpoint availability in Global, US Government L4 and US Government L5 (DOD), but not China operated by 21Vianet.' Both cited pages were read and their availability statements differ.

claims.claim: The web-search setting in Copilot settings links to creating a cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: Follow the link from Copilot settings to create an **Allow web search in Copilot** cloud policy in the [Microsoft 365 Apps admin center]

claims.claim: An appropriate role such as AI Administrator is used to manage Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center, use an appropriate admin role, such as **AI Administrator**.

claims.claim: The Copilot settings page says creating Cloud Policy settings requires the Office Apps admin role.
claims.quote: For example, creating Cloud Policy settings for Microsoft 365 apps requires the **Office Apps admin** role.
claims.fix: Use 'Microsoft's Copilot settings page names the Office Apps admin role for creating Cloud Policy settings. The Cloud Policy overview recommends Office Apps Administrator and also lists Security Administrator and Global Administrator as supported roles.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy, whose role table gives those alternatives, and replace the unqualified 'needs the Office Apps admin role' wording in Governance controls.

claims.claim: Copilot web search generates a short query from a user's prompt and sends it to Bing.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: The web-search request also sends the user's client IP address to Bing.
claims.quote: When Copilot sends a web search request to the Bing search service, it also sends the user's client IP address

claims.claim: The generated web-search query does not include entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote:
The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service:

- The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")
- Entire Microsoft 365 files

claims.claim: A generated web-search query may be informed by an open Microsoft 365 document when prompting inside an app.
claims.quote:
it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document under the following conditions:

- When a user enters a prompt into Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 application

claims.claim: The Data Protection Addendum does not apply to generated web-search queries.
claims.quote: The [Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA)] doesn't apply to the use of generated web search queries in Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Chat, or the Bing search service.

claims.claim: HIPAA compliance does not apply to generated search queries.
claims.quote: Also, HIPAA compliance and the [EU Data Boundary] don't apply to generated search queries.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: A user-level Web content control exists in the Microsoft Copilot app.
claims.quote: The **Web content** toggle gives users control over whether Microsoft Copilot includes real-time web content in responses and is now available to both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat users.

claims.claim: An administrator enabling web search still leaves users able to turn it off for themselves.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns on web search for Microsoft Copilot users, those users still have the option to turn off web search by using the Web content toggle.

claims.claim: When an administrator turns web search off, the Web content toggle is off and dimmed and users cannot enable it.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns off web search, the **Web content** toggle is turned off and appears dimmed. Users can't turn on the toggle to use web search.

claims.claim: For the listed commercial scope, an unconfigured web-search policy leaves web search available unless the optional connected experiences policy is disabled.
claims.quote: If the IT admin doesn't configure the **Allow web search in Copilot** policy, web search will be available to users in both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, unless the IT admin has set the **Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office** policy to **Disabled**.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe an approval step before this feature uses web content.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Copilot web sources approval source references retention'. Read release-notes entry 555896 and returned excerpts; the documented flow requests a presentation then reviews generated slides and source references, with no prior approval step stated.

claims.claim: The release notes do not state how long source references remain in the presentation file.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Copilot web sources approval source references retention'. Read the complete release-note entry for 555896; no duration for references in the file is given. Returned Copilot retention guidance concerns interaction messages, not the presentation's contents.
